{{More footnotes|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Unreferenced|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Infobox deity | Name = Munakata Sanjoshin | image = File:Okinoshima Munakata theology.svg | image_size = | caption = An illustration of the Munakata Sanjoshin in the underpass of {{ill|Miyajimaguchi Station|ja|宮島口駅}} | Gen = | Prev = | Next = | type = {{ill|Kunitsukami|ja|国津神}} (At {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}} and related shrines such as {{ill|Miketsukuni Munakata Jinja|ja|some shrine}}, they are considered protective ancestral deities of the Imperial family and thus {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神}}.) | Fully = | Other_names = | Alias = | Deified_status = Dōshunushi (道主貴) | Deified_nature = Deities of all "paths," worshipped for maritime safety, traffic safety, etc. | temples = {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社}}, {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐八幡宮}}, <!--{{ill|Ōjin Soko Jinja|ja|大神祖神社}},--> {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮}}, {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|ja|鶴岡八幡宮}} }}
[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft|}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神}}.

Toyooka City, Hyogo Prefecture * {{ill|Achi Shrine (Kurashiki)|ja|阿智神社 (倉敷市)}} - Kurashiki City, Okayama Prefecture * {{ill|Kameyama Shrine|ja|亀山神社}} - Mihara City, Hiroshima Prefecture * {{ill|Nichishō Hachiman Shrine|ja|日招八幡大神社}} - Nagasaki City, Nagasaki Prefecture * {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}} - Across Japan * {{ill|Awa no Ōji Shrine|ja|粟皇子神社}} - Futami Town, Ise City, Mie Prefecture
Shrines dedicated primarily to Tagorihime-no-Mikoto: * {{ill|Okitsu Shrine (Munakata)|ja|宗像大社沖津宮}} - Munakata City, Fukuoka Prefecture * {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社}} - Nikkō City, Tochigi Prefecture * {{ill|Takio Shrine|ja|瀧尾神社}} - Various locations in Tochigi Prefecture * {{ill|Amido Shrine|ja|網戸神社}} - Oyama City, Tochigi Prefecture * {{ill|Okitsu Munakata Shrine|ja|興津宗像神社}} - Shimizu-ku, Shizuoka City * {{ill|Fukajima Shrine|ja|深島神社}} - Kita-ku, Nagoya City, Aichi Prefecture
Shrines dedicated primarily to Takitsuhime-no-Mikoto: * {{ill|Nakatsu Shrine (Munakata)|ja|宗像大社中津宮}} - Ōshima, Munakata City, Fukuoka Prefecture * {{ill|Iwaki Shrine|ja|岩木山神社}} - Hirosaki City, Aomori Prefecture
Shrines dedicated primarily to Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto: * {{ill|Hetsu Shrine (Munakata)|ja|宗像大社辺津宮}} - Munakata City, Fukuoka Prefecture * {{ill|Ichikishima Shrine|ja|市杵島神社}} - Across Japan
Shrines jointly enshrining all three goddesses: * {{ill|Tajima Shrine (Imari)|ja|田嶋神社}} - Imari City, Saga Prefecture
Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto is often equated with Benzaiten through {{ill|Honji suijaku|ja|本地垂迹}}. Many shrines originally dedicated to Benzaiten were rededicated to Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto after the Meiji period. * {{ill|Benzaiten Shrine|ja|弁財天宮}} - Shingoto Town, Nagasaki Prefecture * {{ill|Zeniarai Benzaiten Ugafuku Shrine|ja|銭洗弁財天宇賀福神社}} - Kamakura City, Kanagawa Prefecture

== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神}}.

{{More footnotes|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Unreferenced|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Infobox deity | Name = Munakata Sanjoshin | image = File:Okinoshima Munakata theology.svg | image_size = | caption = An illustration of the Munakata Sanjoshin in the underpass of {{ill|Miyajimaguchi Station|ja|宮島口駅}} | Gen = | Prev = | Next = | type = {{ill|Kunitsukami|ja|国津神}} (At {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}} and related shrines such as {{ill|Miketsukuni Munakata Jinja|ja|some shrine}}, they are considered protective ancestral deities of the Imperial family and thus {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神}}.) | Fully = | Other_names = | Alias = | Deified_status = Dōshunushi (道主貴) | Deified_nature = Deities of all "paths," worshipped for maritime safety, traffic safety, etc. | temples = {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社}}, {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐八幡宮}}, <!--{{ill|Ōjin Soko Jinja|ja|大神祖神社}},--> {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮}}, {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|ja|鶴岡八幡宮}} }}
[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft|}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神}}.

[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft|}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神}}.

[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft|}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神}}.

The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft|}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神}}.

[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|12=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|12=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|12=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|12=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|12=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||12=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|12=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|12=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|12=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|12=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=draft}}.

== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=draft}}. Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=draft}}.

The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|12=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|12=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|12=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|12=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||12=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|12=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)

{{More footnotes|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Unreferenced|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Infobox deity | Name = Munakata Sanjoshin | image = File:Okinoshima Munakata theology.svg | image_size = | caption = An illustration of the Munakata Sanjoshin in the underpass of {{ill|Miyajimaguchi Station|ja|宮島口駅|12=draft}} | Gen = | Prev = | Next = | type = {{ill|Kunitsukami|ja|国津神|12=draft}} (At {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft}} and related shrines such as {{ill|Miketsukuni Munakata Jinja|ja|some shrine|12=draft}}, they are considered protective ancestral deities of the Imperial family and thus {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|12=draft}}.) | Fully = | Other_names = | Alias = | Deified_status = Dōshunushi (道主貴) | Deified_nature = Deities of all "paths," worshipped for maritime safety, traffic safety, etc. | temples = {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐八幡宮|12=draft}}, <!--{{ill|Ōjin Soko Jinja|ja|大神祖神社|12=draft}},--> {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|ja|鶴岡八幡宮|12=draft}} }}
[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|12=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|12=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|12=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|12=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|12=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||12=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|12=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|12=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|12=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|12=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=draft}}.

Mihara City, Hiroshima Prefecture * {{ill|Nichishō Hachiman Shrine|ja|日招八幡大神社|12=draft}} - Matsuyama City, Ehime Prefecture * {{ill|Gamo Hachiman Shrine|ja|蒲生八幡神社|12=draft}} - Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu City, Fukuoka Prefecture * {{ill|Rokutake Shrine|ja|六嶽神社|12=draft}} - {{More footnotes|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Unreferenced|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Infobox deity | Name = Munakata Sanjoshin | image = File:Okinoshima Munakata theology.svg | image_size = | caption = An illustration of the Munakata Sanjoshin in the underpass of {{ill|Miyajimaguchi Station|ja|宮島口駅|12=draft}} | Gen = | Prev = | Next = | type = {{ill|Kunitsukami|ja|国津神|12=draft}} (At {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft}} and related shrines such as {{ill|Miketsukuni Munakata Jinja|ja|some shrine|12=draft}}, they are considered protective ancestral deities of the Imperial family and thus {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|12=draft}}.) | Fully = | Other_names = | Alias = | Deified_status = Dōshunushi (道主貴) | Deified_nature = Deities of all "paths," worshipped for maritime safety, traffic safety, etc. | temples = {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐八幡宮|12=draft}}, <!--{{ill|Ōjin Soko Jinja|ja|大神祖神社|12=draft}},--> {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|ja|鶴岡八幡宮|12=draft}} }}
[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|12=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|12=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|12=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|12=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|12=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||12=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|12=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|12=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|12=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|12=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=draft}}.

The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft|12=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|12=draft|12=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft|12=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|12=draft|12=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|12=draft|12=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|12=draft|12=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=draft|12=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=draft|12=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=draft|12=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|12=draft|12=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|12=draft|12=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=draft|12=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=draft|12=draft}}.

{{More footnotes|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Unreferenced|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Infobox deity | Name = Munakata Sanjoshin | image = File:Okinoshima Munakata theology.svg | image_size = | caption = An illustration of the Munakata Sanjoshin in the underpass of {{ill|Miyajimaguchi Station|ja|宮島口駅|12=draft|12=draft}} | Gen = | Prev = | Next = | type = {{ill|Kunitsukami|ja|国津神|12=draft|12=draft}} (At {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}} and related shrines such as {{ill|Miketsukuni Munakata Jinja|ja|some shrine|12=draft|12=draft}}, they are considered protective ancestral deities of the Imperial family and thus {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|12=draft|12=draft}}.) | Fully = | Other_names = | Alias = | Deified_status = Dōshunushi (道主貴) | Deified_nature = Deities of all "paths," worshipped for maritime safety, traffic safety, etc. | temples = {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐八幡宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|ja|鶴岡八幡宮|12=draft|12=draft}} }}
[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|12=draft|12=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft|12=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|12=draft|12=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft|12=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|12=draft|12=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|12=draft|12=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|12=draft|12=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=draft|12=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=draft|12=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=draft|12=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|12=draft|12=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|12=draft|12=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=draft|12=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=draft|12=draft}}.

The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft|12=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|12=draft|12=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft|12=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|12=draft|12=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|12=draft|12=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|12=draft|12=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=draft|12=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=draft|12=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=draft|12=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|12=draft|12=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|12=draft|12=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=draft|12=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=draft|12=draft}}.

[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
