== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

{{脚注の不足|date=2021年6月}} {{Unreferenced|date=2021年6月}} {{基礎情報 日本の神 | 名 = 宗像三女神 | 画像 = | 画像サイズ = | 画像説明 = [[宮島口駅]]の地下道にある宗像三女神のイラスト | 世代名 = | 先代= | 次代= | 神祇 = 国津神 （宗像大社、および京都の宗像神社などでは皇室の守り神、先祖神として「天津神」とする） | 全名 = | 別名 = | 別称 = | 神階 = 道主貴 | 神格 = 交通安全、金運、芸能の神様 | 陵所 = | 父 = [[須佐之男命]]（誓約は婚姻ではないため父、母、とするのは不適当。「物實」としての神の子である） | 母 = [[天照大御神]] | 親 = | 配偶者 = | 子 = | 宮 = | 神社 = [[宗像大社]]、[[厳島神社]]、[[宇佐八幡宮]]、[[宇佐八幡宮#祭神|大神祖神社]]、[[石清水八幡宮]]、[[鶴岡八幡宮]] }} [[Image:Challenge of Amaterashu and Susanoo.svg|thumb|right|240px|アマテラスとスサノヲの誓約（『古事記』に基づく） [[メディア:Challenge of Amaterashu and Susanoo.svg|SVGで表示（対応ブラウザのみ）]]]] '''宗像三女神'''（むなかたさんじょしん）は、[[宗像大社]]（[[福岡県]][[宗像市]]）を総本宮として、日本全国各地に祀られている三柱の[[女神]]の総称である。[[記紀]]に於いて[[アマテラスとスサノオの誓約]]で生まれた女神らで'''宗像大神'''（むなかたのおおかみ）、'''道主貴'''（みちぬしのむち）とも呼ばれ、あらゆる「道」の最高神として[[航海]]の[[安全]]や[[交通安全]]などを祈願する神様として崇敬を集めている。
== 概要 == この三女神は、日本から大陸及び古代朝鮮半島への海上交通の平安を守護する神。海北道中の島々（沖津宮・[[沖ノ島]]、中津宮・[[大島 (福岡県)|筑前大島]]）と辺津宮・[[宗像]]田島に祀られ、[[ヤマト王権|大和朝廷]]によって古くから重視された神々。ムナカタの表記は、『記・紀』では胸形・胸肩・宗形の文字で表している。
アマテラスが国つくりの前（[[天孫降臨]]より以前）、「'''[[うけい]]'''」により生まれたこの三女神に対し「九州から半島、大陸へつながる海の道（海北道中）へ降りて、歴代の[[天皇]]を助けると共に歴代の天皇から篤い祭りを受けよ」と'''[[神勅]]'''を示した。このことから、三女神は現在のそれぞれの地に降臨し、祀されるようになった。これが宗像大社が祀る、沖津宮の「'''田心姫神'''（[[タキリビメ|タゴリヒメ]]）」、中津宮の「'''湍津姫神'''（[[タギツヒメ]]）」、辺津宮の「'''市杵島姫神'''（[[イチキシマヒメ]]）」である。古代、畿内から九州を経由し渡海した[[遣隋使]]や[[遣唐使]]、[[遣新羅使]]もこの海北道中の島々を目印としていた記録が宗像大社神宝館の説明にある。
この三女神はアマテラスとスサノヲの誓（うけい）の結果から生まれたという。スサノヲの邪心を疑ったアマテラスは彼の本心を確かめるために誓約する。スサノヲがたばさんでいる剣を天の真名井ですすぎ、口で噛みくだいてキリとして吐き出した。そうして生まれたという。娘たちに「あなたたち三神は、道中（みちなか）に降臨して天孫を助け奉り、天孫に祭（いつ）かれよ」と命じた。道中とは[[玄界灘]]である<ref>[[藤原新也]]・[[安部龍太郎]]『神の島 沖ノ島』（[[小学館]] 2013年）p.106.</ref>。
『[[古事記]]』神代上巻に「この三柱の神は、胸形君等のもち拝（いつ）く三前（みまえ）の大神なり」とあり、元来は[[宗像氏]]（胸形氏）ら[[筑紫]]（九州北部）の[[海人族]]が古代より集団で祀る神であったとされる。海を隔てた大陸や半島との関係が緊密化（[[神功皇后]]による[[三韓征伐]]など）により土着神であった三神が[[4世紀]]以降、国家神として祭られるようになったとされる。
『[[日本書紀]]』については、卷第一・神代上・第六段の「本文」とその「一書」で[[アマテラスとスサノヲの誓約#日本書紀|天照大神と素戔嗚尊の誓約]]の内容が多少異なる。最初の降臨地は、[[福岡県]]の[[宗像地方]]東端の[[鞍手郡]][[鞍手町]]の[[六ヶ岳]]という[[山]]で、[[筑紫国造]]の田道命の子孫、長田彦（小狭田彦）が、天照大神の神勅をうけて[[神籬]]を建てたのが祭祀の始まり。『宗像大菩薩御縁起「筑前国風土記逸文」』<ref>宗像大社所蔵</ref>『香月文書』<ref name="#1">鞍手町『鞍手町誌』1974年</ref>『六ケ岳神社記』<ref name="#1"/>『福岡県神社誌』<ref>大日本神祇会福岡県支部 『福岡県神社誌』1944年</ref>など。天照大神が「汝三神（いましみはしらのかみ）、道の中に降りて居（ま）して天孫（あめみま）を助け奉（まつ）りて、天孫の為に祭られよ」との神勅を授けたと記されている。これは現代まで祭祀が続く御神名とその鎮座地が明確に記載される記述では、最も古い。
なお、第三の「一書」では、この三女神は先ず筑紫の宇佐嶋の御許山に降臨し宗像の島々に遷座されたとあり、[[宇佐神宮]]では本殿二之御殿に祀られ、この日本書紀の記述を神社年表の始まりとしている。[[八幡神]]の[[比売大神]]である。
別称の「道主貴」の「ムチ」は「貴い神」を表す尊称とされ、神名に「ムチ」が附く神は道主貴のほかには'''[[大日孁貴]]'''（オホヒルメノムチ、天照大神）、'''[[大己貴命]]'''（オホナムチ、大国主）のわずかしか見られない<ref name=tsugita>次田潤『新版祝詞新講』p.506、戎光祥出版、2008年。</ref>。
== 化生した順 == ===『古事記』=== [[古事記|『古事記』]]では、化生した順に以下の三神としている。 * [[沖ノ島]]の沖津宮 - [[タキリビメ|多紀理毘売命]]（たぎりひめ） 別名 奥津島比売命（おきつしまひめ） * [[大島 (福岡県)|大島]]の中津宮 - [[イチキシマヒメ|市寸島比売命]]（いちきしまひめ） 別名 狭依毘売（さよりびめ） * 田島の辺津宮（へつみや） - [[タギツヒメ|多岐都比売命]]（たぎつひめ）
この三社を総称して[[宗像三社]]と呼んでいる。
===『日本書紀』=== [[日本書紀|『日本書紀』]]では以下のようになっている。 * 本文 **沖津宮 - 田心姫（たごりひめ） **中津宮 - 湍津姫（たぎつひめ） **辺津宮 - 市杵嶋姫（いちきしまひめ） * 第一の一書 **沖津宮 - 瀛津嶋姫（おきつしまひめ） **中津宮 - 湍津姫（たぎつひめ） **辺津宮 - 田心姫（たごりひめ） * 第二の一書 **沖津宮 - 市杵嶋姫（いちきしまひめ） **中津宮 - 田心姫（たごりひめ） **辺津宮 - 湍津姫（たぎつひめ） * 第三の一書 **沖津宮 - 瀛津嶋姫（おきつしまひめ） 別名 市杵嶋姫（いちきしまひめ） **中津宮 - 湍津姫（たぎつひめ） **辺津宮 - 田霧姫（たぎりひめ）
[[玄界灘]]に浮かぶ[[沖ノ島]]は[[世界文化遺産]]に登録され、島には沖津宮があり田心姫神を祀っている。島には古代祭祀遺構があり出土品は一括して[[国宝]]に指定されている（邊津宮にある宗像大社神宝館にて展示されている）。
=== 宗像大社の社伝 === 宗像大社の社伝では、以下のようになっている（三女神の神名や配列などに 古来、種々の変遷もあったが現在では以下のようになっている）。 * 沖津宮 - 田心姫神（たごりひめ） * 中津宮 - 湍津姫神（たぎつひめ） * 辺津宮 - 市杵島姫神（いちきしまひめ）
== 宗像三女神を祭神とする全国の神社 == 海の神・航海の神として信仰されている。宗像大社のほか各地の宗像神社・[[宮地嶽神社]]・[[厳島神社]]・[[八王子社]]・[[天真名井社]]・[[石神神社]]などで祀られている。[[八幡社]]の[[比売大神]]としても[[宇佐神宮]]や[[石清水八幡宮]]で祀られている。
宗像系の神社は日本で5番目に多いとされ、そのほとんどが大和及び伊勢、志摩から熊野灘、瀬戸内海を通って大陸へ行く経路に沿った所にある。なお、[[八王子神社]]は[[五男三女神]]を祀る神社である。
=== 神社一覧 === '''[[宗像大社]]''' - 福岡県宗像市田島鎮座 総本社 *[[宗像神社]] - 全国各地 *[[厳島神社]] - 広島県廿日市市厳島鎮座 安芸国一宮 **[[厳島神社 (曖昧さ回避)|厳島神社]] - 全国各地 *[[網走神社]] - 北海道網走市鎮座 北見国一宮 *[[善知鳥神社]] - 青森県青森市安方鎮座 *[[八戸三嶋神社]] - 青森県八戸市鎮座 *[[隠津島神社 (郡山市湖南町福良)]] - 福島県郡山市湖南町鎮座 *[[隠津島神社 (二本松市)]] - 福島県二本松市木幡鎮座 *[[都野神社]] - 新潟県長岡市鎮座 *[[江島神社]] - 神奈川県藤沢市江の島鎮座 *[[前川神社]] - 埼玉県川口市鎮座 *[[天宮神社]] - 静岡県周智郡森町天宮鎮座 *[[藤切神社]] - 滋賀県東近江市甲津畑町鎮座 *[[阿自岐神社]] - 滋賀県鎮座 *[[市比賣神社]] - 京都市下京区河原町鎮座 *[[繁昌神社]] - 京都市下京区繁昌町鎮座 *[[日向大神宮]] - 京都市山科区鎮座 *[[八坂神社]][[美御前社]] - 京都八坂神社内末社 *[[穴水大宮]] - 石川県穴水町鎮座 *[[四所神社 (豊岡市)]] - 兵庫県豊岡市鎮座 *[[阿智神社 (倉敷市)]] - 岡山県倉敷市本町鎮座 *[[亀山神社]] - 広島県三原市鎮座 *[[岩國白蛇神社]] - 山口県岩国市鎮座 *[[日招八幡大神社]] - 愛媛県松山市鎮座 *[[蒲生八幡神社]] - 福岡県北九州市小倉南区蒲生鎮座 *[[六嶽神社]] - 福岡県鞍手町六ヶ岳鎮座 *[[慈島宮]]（厳島神社に改名） - 福岡県宗像市地島鎮座 *[[七夕神社]] - 福岡県小郡市大崎鎮座 *[[薦神社]] - 大分県中津市鎮座 *[[田島神社]]- 佐賀県唐津市呼子町加部島鎮座 *[[淵神社]] - 長崎県長崎市淵町鎮座 *[[須賀神社]]（須加神社） - 東京都・三重県・兵庫県・佐賀県など各地に鎮座 *[[粟皇子神社]] - 三重県伊勢市二見町松下字鳥取に鎮座 （[[神宮125社の一覧|神宮125社]]の一つ）
宗像三女神のうち、田心姫神を主祭神とする神社。 *宗像大社沖津宮 - 福岡県宗像市沖ノ島鎮座 *[[日光二荒山神社]] - 栃木県日光市鎮座 *[[瀧尾神社 (曖昧さ回避)|瀧尾神社]] - 栃木県宇都宮市等各所鎮座 *[[網戸神社]] - 栃木県小山市鎮座 *[[興津宗像神社]] - 静岡県静岡市清水区興津中町鎮座 *[[深島神社]] - 愛知県名古屋市北区柳原鎮座 *[[瀧浪神社]] - 石川県小松市鎮座 *[[小汐井神社]] - 滋賀県草津市大路鎮座 *[[新日吉神宮]] - 京都府京都市東山区鎮座 *[[一宮神社 (神戸市)]] - 兵庫県神戸市中央区山本通鎮座 生田裔神八社の1社 *[[津門神社]] - 島根県江津市波子町鎮座
宗像三女神のうち、湍津姫神を主祭神とする神社。 *宗像大社中津宮 - 福岡県宗像市大島鎮座 *[[岩木山神社]] - 青森県弘前市百沢鎮座 津軽国一宮 *[[石峰山石神社]] - 宮城県石巻市雄勝町鎮座 *[[高津比咩神社]] - 千葉県八千代市高津鎮座 *[[奥津嶋神社]] - 滋賀県近江八幡市沖島町鎮座 *[[大嶋神社奥津嶋神社]] - 滋賀県近江八幡市北津田町鎮座 *[[三宮神社 (神戸市)]] - 兵庫県神戸市中央区三宮町鎮座 生田裔神八社の1社

{{More footnotes|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Unreferenced|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Infobox deity | Name = Munakata Sanjoshin | image = File:Okinoshima Munakata theology.svg | image_size = | caption = An illustration of the Munakata Sanjoshin in the underpass of {{ill|Miyajimaguchi Station|ja|宮島口駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Gen = | Prev = | Next = | type = {{ill|Kunitsukami|ja|国津神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (At {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and related shrines such as {{ill|Miketsukuni Munakata Jinja|ja|some shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are considered protective ancestral deities of the Imperial family and thus {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.) | Fully = | Other_names = | Alias = | Deified_status = Dōshunushi (道主貴) | Deified_nature = Deities of all "paths," worshipped for maritime safety, traffic safety, etc. | temples = {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|ja|鶴岡八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }}
[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

{{脚注の不足|date=2021年6月}} {{Unreferenced|date=2021年6月}} {{基礎情報 日本の神 | 名 = 宗像三女神 | 画像 = | 画像サイズ = | 画像説明 = [[宮島口駅]]の地下道にある宗像三女神のイラスト | 世代名 = | 先代= | 次代= | 神祇 = 国津神 （宗像大社、および京都の宗像神社などでは皇室の守り神、先祖神として「天津神」とする） | 全名 = | 別名 = | 別称 = | 神階 = 道主貴 | 神格 = 交通安全、金運、芸能の神様 | 陵所 = | 父 = [[須佐之男命]]（誓約は婚姻ではないため父、母、とするのは不適当。「物實」としての神の子である） | 母 = [[天照大御神]] | 親 = | 配偶者 = | 子 = | 宮 = | 神社 = [[宗像大社]]、[[厳島神社]]、[[宇佐八幡宮]]、[[宇佐八幡宮#祭神|大神祖神社]]、[[石清水八幡宮]]、[[鶴岡八幡宮]] }} [[Image:Challenge of Amaterashu and Susanoo.svg|thumb|right|240px|アマテラスとスサノヲの誓約（『古事記』に基づく） [[メディア:Challenge of Amaterashu and Susanoo.svg|SVGで表示（対応ブラウザのみ）]]]] '''宗像三女神'''（むなかたさんじょしん）は、[[宗像大社]]（[[福岡県]][[宗像市]]）を総本宮として、日本全国各地に祀られている三柱の[[女神]]の総称である。[[記紀]]に於いて[[アマテラスとスサノオの誓約]]で生まれた女神らで'''宗像大神'''（むなかたのおおかみ）、'''道主貴'''（みちぬしのむち）とも呼ばれ、あらゆる「道」の最高神として[[航海]]の[[安全]]や[[交通安全]]などを祈願する神様として崇敬を集めている。
== 概要 == この三女神は、日本から大陸及び古代朝鮮半島への海上交通の平安を守護する神。海北道中の島々（沖津宮・[[沖ノ島]]、中津宮・[[大島 (福岡県)|筑前大島]]）と辺津宮・[[宗像]]田島に祀られ、[[ヤマト王権|大和朝廷]]によって古くから重視された神々。ムナカタの表記は、『記・紀』では胸形・胸肩・宗形の文字で表している。
アマテラスが国つくりの前（[[天孫降臨]]より以前）、「'''[[うけい]]'''」により生まれたこの三女神に対し「九州から半島、大陸へつながる海の道（海北道中）へ降りて、歴代の[[天皇]]を助けると共に歴代の天皇から篤い祭りを受けよ」と'''[[神勅]]'''を示した。このことから、三女神は現在のそれぞれの地に降臨し、祀されるようになった。これが宗像大社が祀る、沖津宮の「'''田心姫神'''（[[タキリビメ|タゴリヒメ]]）」、中津宮の「'''湍津姫神'''（[[タギツヒメ]]）」、辺津宮の「'''市杵島姫神'''（[[イチキシマヒメ]]）」である。古代、畿内から九州を経由し渡海した[[遣隋使]]や[[遣唐使]]、[[遣新羅使]]もこの海北道中の島々を目印としていた記録が宗像大社神宝館の説明にある。
この三女神はアマテラスとスサノヲの誓（うけい）の結果から生まれたという。スサノヲの邪心を疑ったアマテラスは彼の本心を確かめるために誓約する。スサノヲがたばさんでいる剣を天の真名井ですすぎ、口で噛みくだいてキリとして吐き出した。そうして生まれたという。娘たちに「あなたたち三神は、道中（みちなか）に降臨して天孫を助け奉り、天孫に祭（いつ）かれよ」と命じた。道中とは[[玄界灘]]である<ref>[[藤原新也]]・[[安部龍太郎]]『神の島 沖ノ島』（[[小学館]] 2013年）p.106.</ref>。
『[[古事記]]』神代上巻に「この三柱の神は、胸形君等のもち拝（いつ）く三前（みまえ）の大神なり」とあり、元来は[[宗像氏]]（胸形氏）ら[[筑紫]]（九州北部）の[[海人族]]が古代より集団で祀る神であったとされる。海を隔てた大陸や半島との関係が緊密化（[[神功皇后]]による[[三韓征伐]]など）により土着神であった三神が[[4世紀]]以降、国家神として祭られるようになったとされる。
『[[日本書紀]]』については、卷第一・神代上・第六段の「本文」とその「一書」で[[アマテラスとスサノヲの誓約#日本書紀|天照大神と素戔嗚尊の誓約]]の内容が多少異なる。最初の降臨地は、[[福岡県]]の[[宗像地方]]東端の[[鞍手郡]][[鞍手町]]の[[六ヶ岳]]という[[山]]で、[[筑紫国造]]の田道命の子孫、長田彦（小狭田彦）が、天照大神の神勅をうけて[[神籬]]を建てたのが祭祀の始まり。『宗像大菩薩御縁起「筑前国風土記逸文」』<ref>宗像大社所蔵</ref>『香月文書』<ref name="#1">鞍手町『鞍手町誌』1974年</ref>『六ケ岳神社記』<ref name="#1"/>『福岡県神社誌』<ref>大日本神祇会福岡県支部 『福岡県神社誌』1944年</ref>など。天照大神が「汝三神（いましみはしらのかみ）、道の中に降りて居（ま）して天孫（あめみま）を助け奉（まつ）りて、天孫の為に祭られよ」との神勅を授けたと記されている。これは現代まで祭祀が続く御神名とその鎮座地が明確に記載される記述では、最も古い。
なお、第三の「一書」では、この三女神は先ず筑紫の宇佐嶋の御許山に降臨し宗像の島々に遷座されたとあり、[[宇佐神宮]]では本殿二之御殿に祀られ、この日本書紀の記述を神社年表の始まりとしている。[[八幡神]]の[[比売大神]]である。
別称の「道主貴」の「ムチ」は「貴い神」を表す尊称とされ、神名に「ムチ」が附く神は道主貴のほかには'''[[大日孁貴]]'''（オホヒルメノムチ、天照大神）、'''[[大己貴命]]'''（オホナムチ、大国主）のわずかしか見られない<ref name=tsugita>次田潤『新版祝詞新講』p.506、戎光祥出版、2008年。</ref>。
== 化生した順 == ===『古事記』=== [[古事記|『古事記』]]では、化生した順に以下の三神としている。 * [[沖ノ島]]の沖津宮 - [[タキリビメ|多紀理毘売命]]（たぎりひめ） 別名 奥津島比売命（おきつしまひめ） * [[大島 (福岡県)|大島]]の中津宮 - [[イチキシマヒメ|市寸島比売命]]（いちきしまひめ） 別名 狭依毘売（さよりびめ） * 田島の辺津宮（へつみや） - [[タギツヒメ|多岐都比売命]]（たぎつひめ）
この三社を総称して[[宗像三社]]と呼んでいる。
===『日本書紀』=== [[日本書紀|『日本書紀』]]では以下のようになっている。 * 本文 **沖津宮 - 田心姫（たごりひめ） **中津宮 - 湍津姫（たぎつひめ） **辺津宮 - 市杵嶋姫（いちきしまひめ） * 第一の一書 **沖津宮 - 瀛津嶋姫（おきつしまひめ） **中津宮 - 湍津姫（たぎつひめ） **辺津宮 - 田心姫（たごりひめ） * 第二の一書 **沖津宮 - 市杵嶋姫（いちきしまひめ） **中津宮 - 田心姫（たごりひめ） **辺津宮 - 湍津姫（たぎつひめ） * 第三の一書 **沖津宮 - 瀛津嶋姫（おきつしまひめ） 別名 市杵嶋姫（いちきしまひめ） **中津宮 - 湍津姫（たぎつひめ） **辺津宮 - 田霧姫（たぎりひめ）
[[玄界灘]]に浮かぶ[[沖ノ島]]は[[世界文化遺産]]に登録され、島には沖津宮があり田心姫神を祀っている。島には古代祭祀遺構があり出土品は一括して[[国宝]]に指定されている（邊津宮にある宗像大社神宝館にて展示されている）。
=== 宗像大社の社伝 === 宗像大社の社伝では、以下のようになっている（三女神の神名や配列などに 古来、種々の変遷もあったが現在では以下のようになっている）。 * 沖津宮 - 田心姫神（たごりひめ） * 中津宮 - 湍津姫神（たぎつひめ） * 辺津宮 - 市杵島姫神（いちきしまひめ）
== 宗像三女神を祭神とする全国の神社 == 海の神・航海の神として信仰されている。宗像大社のほか各地の宗像神社・[[宮地嶽神社]]・[[厳島神社]]・[[八王子社]]・[[天真名井社]]・[[石神神社]]などで祀られている。[[八幡社]]の[[比売大神]]としても[[宇佐神宮]]や[[石清水八幡宮]]で祀られている。
宗像系の神社は日本で5番目に多いとされ、そのほとんどが大和及び伊勢、志摩から熊野灘、瀬戸内海を通って大陸へ行く経路に沿った所にある。なお、[[八王子神社]]は[[五男三女神]]を祀る神社である。

[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

{{More footnotes|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Unreferenced|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Infobox deity | Name = Munakata Sanjoshin | image = File:Okinoshima Munakata theology.svg | image_size = | caption = An illustration of the Munakata Sanjoshin in the underpass of {{ill|Miyajimaguchi Station|ja|宮島口駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Gen = | Prev = | Next = | type = {{ill|Kunitsukami|ja|国津神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (At {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and related shrines such as {{ill|Miketsukuni Munakata Jinja|ja|some shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are considered protective ancestral deities of the Imperial family and thus {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.) | Fully = | Other_names = | Alias = | Deified_status = Dōshunushi (道主貴) | Deified_nature = Deities of all "paths," worshipped for maritime safety, traffic safety, etc. | temples = {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|ja|鶴岡八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }}
[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishimahime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishimahime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishimahime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishimahime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishimahime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishimahime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishima-hime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)

{{More footnotes|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Unreferenced|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Infobox deity | Name = Munakata Sanjoshin | image = File:Okinoshima Munakata theology.svg | image_size = | caption = An illustration of the Munakata Sanjoshin in the underpass of {{ill|Miyajimaguchi Station|ja|宮島口駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Gen = | Prev = | Next = | type = {{ill|Kunitsukami|ja|国津神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (At {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and related shrines such as {{ill|Miketsukuni Munakata Jinja|ja|some shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are considered protective ancestral deities of the Imperial family and thus {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.) | Fully = | Other_names = | Alias = | Deified_status = Dōshunushi (道主貴) | Deified_nature = Deities of all "paths," worshipped for maritime safety, traffic safety, etc. | temples = {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|ja|鶴岡八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }}
[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishima-hime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishima-hime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)

[[sn:Three Munakata Goddesses]] [[ja:宗像三女神]]

{{More footnotes|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Unreferenced|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Infobox deity | Name = Munakata Sanjoshin | image = File:Okinoshima Munakata theology.svg | image_size = | caption = An illustration of the Munakata Sanjoshin in the underpass of {{ill|Miyajimaguchi Station|ja|宮島口駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Gen = | Prev = | Next = | type = {{ill|Kunitsukami|ja|国津神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (At {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and related shrines such as {{ill|Miketsukuni Munakata Jinja|ja|some shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are considered protective ancestral deities of the Imperial family and thus {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.) | Fully = | Other_names = | Alias = | Deified_status = Dōshunushi (道主貴) | Deified_nature = Deities of all "paths," worshipped for maritime safety, traffic safety, etc. | temples = {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|ja|鶴岡八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }}
[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishima-hime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishima-hime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)

{{More footnotes|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Unreferenced|date=December 29, 2022}} {{Infobox deity | Name = Munakata Sanjoshin | image = File:Okinoshima Munakata theology.svg | image_size = | caption = An illustration of the Munakata Sanjoshin in the underpass of {{ill|Miyajimaguchi Station|ja|宮島口駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | Gen = | Prev = | Next = | type = {{ill|Kunitsukami|ja|国津神|1=Kunitsukami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (At {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and related shrines such as {{ill|Miketsukuni Munakata Jinja|ja|some shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are considered protective ancestral deities of the Imperial family and thus {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.) | Fully = | Other_names = | Alias = | Deified_status = Dōshunushi (道主貴) | Deified_nature = Deities of all "paths," worshipped for maritime safety, traffic safety, etc. | temples = {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|ja|鶴岡八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} }}
[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft||qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishima-hime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|en:draft||fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.

Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on [[Okinoshima]]: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Taisha|qq=}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Shrines|qq=}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|ja|宮地嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyajidake Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|ja|厳島神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itsukushima Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishigami Shrine|qq=}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Usa Jingū|qq=}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|qq=}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Male and Three Female Gods|qq=}}.
