[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|WD=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha|1=Munakata Taisha}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|en|Munakata, Fukuoka|WD=Q819603|lt=Munakata, Fukuoka|1=Munakata, Fukuoka}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|en|Ukehi|WD=Q11260316|lt=Ukehi|1=Ukehi}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} and {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagorihime|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|qq=}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishima-hime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|qq=}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[:en:Kentōshi|Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on {{ill|Okinoshima|en|Okinoshima|WD=Q353923|lt=Okinoshima|1=Okinoshima}}: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|WD=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha|1=Munakata Taisha}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Shrines|qq=}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|en|Miyajidake Shrine|WD=Q3317296|lt=Miyajidake Shrine|1=Miyajidake Shrine}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|en|Itsukushima Shrine|WD=Q191763|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|1=Itsukushima Shrine}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八王子神社}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishigami Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 比売神}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|en|Usa Jingū|WD=Q715632|lt=Usa Jingū|1=Usa Jingū}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|en|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|WD=Q710098|lt=Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|1=Iwashimizu Hachimangū}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|qq=}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Deities|lt=Five Male and Three Female Deities|lt=Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アマテラスとスサノオの誓約}}.

[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|WD=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha|1=Munakata Taisha}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|en|Munakata, Fukuoka|WD=Q819603|lt=Munakata, Fukuoka|1=Munakata, Fukuoka}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|en|Ukehi|WD=Q11260316|lt=Ukehi|1=Ukehi}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} and {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagorihime|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|qq=}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishima-hime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|qq=}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[:en:Kentōshi|Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on {{ill|Okinoshima|en|Okinoshima|WD=Q353923|lt=Okinoshima|1=Okinoshima}}: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|WD=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha|1=Munakata Taisha}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Shrines|qq=}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|en|Miyajidake Shrine|WD=Q3317296|lt=Miyajidake Shrine|1=Miyajidake Shrine}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|en|Itsukushima Shrine|WD=Q191763|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|1=Itsukushima Shrine}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八王子神社}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishigami Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 比売神}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|en|Usa Jingū|WD=Q715632|lt=Usa Jingū|1=Usa Jingū}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|en|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|WD=Q710098|lt=Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|1=Iwashimizu Hachimangū}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|qq=}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Deities|lt=Five Male and Three Female Deities|lt=Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アマテラスとスサノオの誓約}}.

[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|WD=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha|1=Munakata Taisha}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|en|Munakata, Fukuoka|WD=Q819603|lt=Munakata, Fukuoka|1=Munakata, Fukuoka}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|en|Ukehi|WD=Q11260316|lt=Ukehi|1=Ukehi}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} and {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagorihime|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|qq=}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishima-hime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|qq=}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[:en:Kentōshi|Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on {{ill|Okinoshima|en|Okinoshima|WD=Q353923|lt=Okinoshima|1=Okinoshima}}: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|WD=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha|1=Munakata Taisha}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Shrines|qq=}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|en|Miyajidake Shrine|WD=Q3317296|lt=Miyajidake Shrine|1=Miyajidake Shrine}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|en|Itsukushima Shrine|WD=Q191763|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|1=Itsukushima Shrine}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八王子神社}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishigami Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 比売神}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|en|Usa Jingū|WD=Q715632|lt=Usa Jingū|1=Usa Jingū}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|en|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|WD=Q710098|lt=Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|1=Iwashimizu Hachimangū}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|qq=}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Deities|lt=Five Male and Three Female Deities|lt=Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アマテラスとスサノオの誓約}}.

Hachimangū}}, {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|en|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|WD=Q701403|lt=Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|1=Tsurugaoka Hachimangū}} }}
[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|WD=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha|1=Munakata Taisha}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|en|Munakata, Fukuoka|WD=Q819603|lt=Munakata, Fukuoka|1=Munakata, Fukuoka}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|en|Ukehi|WD=Q11260316|lt=Ukehi|1=Ukehi}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} and {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagorihime|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|qq=}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishima-hime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|qq=}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[:en:Kentōshi|Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on {{ill|Okinoshima|en|Okinoshima|WD=Q353923|lt=Okinoshima|1=Okinoshima}}: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|WD=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha|1=Munakata Taisha}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Shrines|qq=}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|en|Miyajidake Shrine|WD=Q3317296|lt=Miyajidake Shrine|1=Miyajidake Shrine}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|en|Itsukushima Shrine|WD=Q191763|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|1=Itsukushima Shrine}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八王子神社}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishigami Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 比売神}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|en|Usa Jingū|WD=Q715632|lt=Usa Jingū|1=Usa Jingū}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|en|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|WD=Q710098|lt=Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|1=Iwashimizu Hachimangū}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|qq=}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Deities|lt=Five Male and Three Female Deities|lt=Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アマテラスとスサノオの誓約}}.

Hachimangū}}, {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|en|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|WD=Q701403|lt=Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|1=Tsurugaoka Hachimangū}} }}
[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|WD=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha|1=Munakata Taisha}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|en|Munakata, Fukuoka|WD=Q819603|lt=Munakata, Fukuoka|1=Munakata, Fukuoka}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|en|Ukehi|WD=Q11260316|lt=Ukehi|1=Ukehi}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} and {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagorihime|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|qq=}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishima-hime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|qq=}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[:en:Kentōshi|Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on {{ill|Okinoshima|en|Okinoshima|WD=Q353923|lt=Okinoshima|1=Okinoshima}}: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|WD=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha|1=Munakata Taisha}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Shrines|qq=}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|en|Miyajidake Shrine|WD=Q3317296|lt=Miyajidake Shrine|1=Miyajidake Shrine}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|en|Itsukushima Shrine|WD=Q191763|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|1=Itsukushima Shrine}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八王子神社}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishigami Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 比売神}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|en|Usa Jingū|WD=Q715632|lt=Usa Jingū|1=Usa Jingū}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|en|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|WD=Q710098|lt=Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|1=Iwashimizu Hachimangū}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|qq=}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Deities|lt=Five Male and Three Female Deities|lt=Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アマテラスとスサノオの誓約}}.

[[File:Children born from the Challenge of Amaterasu and Susanoo-en.svg|thumb|right|240px|The “Ukehi” (divine oath) between Amaterasu and Susanoo (based on the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}'')]]
The '''Munakata Sanjoshin''' (宗像三女神, "Three Goddesses of Munakata") are three female [[kami]] enshrined primarily at {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|WD=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha|1=Munakata Taisha}} in {{ill|Munakata, Fukuoka|en|Munakata, Fukuoka|WD=Q819603|lt=Munakata, Fukuoka|1=Munakata, Fukuoka}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}} and worshipped at shrines nationwide. According to the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}'' and ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}'', they were born from the {{ill|Ukehi|en|Ukehi|WD=Q11260316|lt=Ukehi|1=Ukehi}} (sacred trial of sincerity) between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} and {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}. Also called '''Munakata Ōkami''' (宗像大神) or '''Dōshunushi''' (道主貴), they are revered as supreme deities of all "paths." They are particularly worshipped for maritime safety and traffic safety.
== Overview == The Munakata Sanjoshin were originally worshipped for safe maritime travel between Japan and the continent (modern China and the Korean Peninsula), protecting the sea route via islands of Okinoshima, Ōshima, and Tashima (Hetsu-miya). This route was crucial in ancient times and recognized by the ancient Yamato court.
Born from the Ukehi between Amaterasu and Susanoo, the three goddesses were commanded by a divine decree from Amaterasu to descend to the "middle of the path" (the seas around Kyushu) to assist the imperial descendants and be worshiped by them. They settled on Okinoshima (Okitsu-miya), Ōshima (Nakatsu-miya), and Tashima (Hetsu-miya) in what is now Fukuoka Prefecture. They have been revered by ancient maritime clans and later by the Yamato state as protectors of overseas voyages. Over time, they became state-protected deities, especially after the 4th century and the rising influence of the Yamato court.
In texts: * In the ''Kojiki'': They are known as {{ill|Tagorihime|ja|タキリビメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagorihime|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|タギツヒメ|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagitsuhime|qq=}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|1=Ichikishima-hime|lt=Ichikishima-hime|simple|User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime|qq=}} * In the ''Nihon Shoki'': Their names and order vary in different versions, but they are associated with the three shrines of Munakata Taisha: Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya.
Known collectively as Munakata Ōkami, their worship spread as maritime routes to the mainland became more important. They were considered protective gods for overseas envoys (e.g., [[:en:Kentōshi|Kentōshi]] missions) and are closely linked to the [[Hachiman]] cult, as one of them (Ichikishima-hime) is also known as Hime-gami (the female deity) of the [[Usa Jingū|Usa Hachiman cult]].
They are one of the few deities whose names receive the honorific "Muchi" (貴), a title shared only by a handful of major deities like {{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi (Amaterasu)|ja|大日孁貴|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}} (Amaterasu) and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi no Mikoto (Ōkuninushi)|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}.<ref name=tsugita>Tsugita Jun, "Shinban norito shinkō," Yuzankaku, 2008, p.506.</ref>
== Order of Birth == === According to the Kojiki === In the ''Kojiki'', they appear in this order: * Okitsu-miya on {{ill|Okinoshima|en|Okinoshima|WD=Q353923|lt=Okinoshima|1=Okinoshima}}: [[Tagirihime no Mikoto|Tagiri-hime]] (also known as Okitsushima-hime) * Nakatsu-miya on [[Ōshima (Fukuoka)|Ōshima]]: Ichikishima-hime (also known as Sayori-bime) * Hetsu-miya in Tashima: Tagitsu-hime
Collectively known as [[Munakata Sansha]] (the three Munakata shrines).
=== According to the Nihon Shoki === The ''Nihon Shoki'' provides several variants (main text and three alternate writings), listing their names and which shrine they correspond to: * Main Text: Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime (田心姫), Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime (湍津姫), Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime (市杵島姫) * Alternate Writings: Names and order vary among Tagori-hime, Tagitsu-hime, and Ichikishima-hime, associated respectively with Okitsu-miya, Nakatsu-miya, and Hetsu-miya in different permutations.
=== Munakata Taisha Tradition === Munakata Taisha's official tradition currently reveres them as: * Okitsu-miya: Tagori-hime no Kami (田心姫神) * Nakatsu-miya: Tagitsu-hime no Kami (湍津姫神) * Hetsu-miya: Ichikishima-hime no Kami (市杵島姫神)
== Shrines Enshrining the Three Munakata Goddesses ==
The Three Munakata Goddesses are worshipped as sea deities and protectors of navigation. In addition to {{ill|Munakata Taisha|en|Munakata Taisha|WD=Q704962|lt=Munakata Taisha|1=Munakata Taisha}}, they are enshrined at various shrines across Japan, including {{ill|Munakata Shrines|ja|宗像神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Shrines|qq=}}, {{ill|Miyajidake Shrine|en|Miyajidake Shrine|WD=Q3317296|lt=Miyajidake Shrine|1=Miyajidake Shrine}}, {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine|en|Itsukushima Shrine|WD=Q191763|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|1=Itsukushima Shrine}}, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八王子神社}}, {{ill|Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja|天真名井社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsu Mana I Well Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Ishigami Shrine|ja|石神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishigami Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. They are also worshipped as {{ill|Himegami|ja|比売大神|lt=Hime-no-Ōkami|1=Himegami|3=比売神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 比売神}} at {{ill|Usa Jingū|en|Usa Jingū|WD=Q715632|lt=Usa Jingū|1=Usa Jingū}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|en|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|WD=Q710098|lt=Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine|1=Iwashimizu Hachimangū}}.
Shrines associated with the Munakata lineage Rank fifth in number across Japan. Most are located along routes from Yamato and Ise through Shima, Kumano-nada, the Seto Inland Sea, and to the continent. Notably, {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|qq=}} enshrines the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Deities|lt=Five Male and Three Female Deities|lt=Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja|五男三女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Male and Three Female Gods|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アマテラスとスサノオの誓約}}.
